name: third_party
summary: Outbound connector fabric. ThirdPartyManager loads configs from studio/third_party/, instantiates per-platform connectors (Discord / Telegram / Twitter / Facebook / WhatsApp), routes messages by tag/tier, and logs every send append-only.
engine_pattern: abstract base.Connector (connect/send/history/disconnect) + per-platform subclasses. Manager is the single dispatch point; tag-routing fans messages out to multiple connectors.

inbound_callers: CLI: python3 third_party_cli.py connect | send | list | status | archive
chat.py (when a chat call needs to surface output to an external channel)
routing_connections.substrate_writes: per-service send logs; inference_logger crystal chain entries (one per send)

merge_with_moe_stack: Every send through ThirdPartyManager logs an InferenceRecord (tier='outbound', model='<service>', original_prompt='<message>', output_text='<delivery_receipt>'). These records become first-class crystal-chain entries — the MoE router can later retrieve past outbound sends as experts when planning new ones.
guarantees: Append-only send log — never edit or delete
Per-host token isolation — auth lives in mode-600 JSON, never committed
Tag-routing is deterministic — same tag set → same recipient set
Disconnected sends fail loudly (do not silently skip)
security_notes: Token rotation: rotated tokens move to studio/third_party/{service}/*.rotated.json (excluded from registry walk)
Phishing surface: third_party.send refuses to send to unverified recipients in the friend registry
usage_example: python3 core/lib/third_party_cli.py connect --service discord --token $DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN --name dev_server --tags 'broadcast,alerts'\npython3 core/lib/third_party_cli.py send --service discord --to channel_123 --message 'build complete'
